scenes.title:
Learn it once.
Write it in **any language**.
scenes.sub: Every language does the same things. Only the words you type change.
say: Every language can do the same things. Only the words you type are different.

say.say: So learn the idea once, in pseudocode, and look up the words in your language.

items.text:
Java        new HashMap<>()
Python      {}
C++         unordered_map<string, int>
JavaScript  new Map()
Same steps. Same Big-O. Different words.

say.say: Take one pseudocode line: m equals an empty map.
In Java it's a HashMap. In Python, a dict. In C plus plus, an unordered map. In JavaScript, a Map.
What it does, the steps you write, and what it costs, stay the same in all four.

scenes.label: ARRAY
scenes.title: A list that grows
head: PSEUDOCODE

say.say: Arrays first. Appending 7 is add in Java, append in Python, push back in C plus plus, and push in JavaScript.

say: Reading the first item is a bracket with index 0 everywhere, except a Java list, which uses get.
And the length: size, len, size, and length.

scenes.label: HASH MAP
scenes.title: Key in, value out
head: PSEUDOCODE
JAVA
PYTHON
C++
JAVASCRIPT

note.text: In JavaScript, use a `Map`, not a plain object: it takes keys of any type and has `has()` built in.

say.say: A hash map. Storing a value is put in Java, and set in JavaScript. Python and C plus plus use brackets.

say: Reading it back: get, or brackets.
Checking for a key: contains key, the word in, count greater than zero, and has.

say.say: In JavaScript, use a real Map rather than a plain object. It takes keys of any type.

scenes.title: Have I seen it?
head: PSEUDOCODE
JAVA
PYTHON
C++

say: A set. Adding is add, except C plus plus, which says insert.
Checking is contains, in, count, or has.

say.say: Removing is remove, remove, erase, and delete.

scenes.label: STACK
scenes.title: Last in, first out
head: PSEUDOCODE
JAVA
PYTHON
C++
JAVASCRIPT

say.say: A stack. In Java, use an ArrayDeque. Python and JavaScript use a plain list, or array.

say: Looking at the top: peek, the last index, top, and the last index again.

say.say: Pop looks the same in all four. But it doesn't behave the same. Hold that thought.

scenes.label: QUEUE
scenes.title: First in, first out
head: PSEUDOCODE
JAVA
PYTHON
C++
JAVASCRIPT

say.say: A queue. Join at the back: offer, append, push, push.

say: Look at the front: peek, index 0, front, and index head in JavaScript.

say.say: Leave from the front: poll, pop left, pop, and head plus plus. In Python, the deque comes from the collections module.
say.show: Leave from the front: poll, popleft, pop, and head++. In Python, deque comes from the collections module.

say.say: Here's that thought. In C plus plus, pop removes the top, but returns nothing. This line won't compile.
say.show: Here's that thought. In C++, pop() removes the top, but returns nothing. This line won't compile.

say.say: Read the top first, then pop. The same goes for a queue's front.
Here's a question. Does JavaScript have a queue? No. Shift removes the front, but moves every other item along. That's O of n, per removal.
say.show: Here's a question. Does JavaScript have a queue? No. shift() removes the front, but moves every other item along. That's O(n), per removal.

say.say: Keep a head index instead. Reading the front and moving head forward is O of 1.
say.show: Keep a head index instead. q[head++] reads the front and moves head forward: O(1).

say.say: JavaScript has no queue, so most code does this: shift off the front.
say.show: JavaScript has no queue, so a lot of code does this: shift() off the front.

say.say: But shift moves every other item one place along. That's O of n, every time.
say.show: But shift() moves every other item one place along. That's O(n), every time.

say.say: Keep an index for the front, starting at zero.
Read the front with head, then move head forward. Nothing shifts. O of 1.
say.show: Read q[head], then move head forward. Nothing shifts. O(1).

say.say: Joining the back is still push.
say.show: Joining the back is still push().
